skill.displayName: Pet Body Condition Score 3D Analysis | 宠物体态3D评分（BCS）

llm.summary: This skill performs the advertised pet video analysis, but it also silently creates or reuses an account identity and stores authentication state for cloud history access.

dimensions.detail: Reading local video files and sending URLs or media to a backend is purpose-aligned, but workspace data files, SQLite user records, and stored tokens are broader than a simple one-shot media analysis flow.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No post-install hook or remote code execution was found; the package ships Python modules, pinned dependencies, and service configuration for lifeemergence.com endpoints.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill tells the agent not to ask for or reveal internal identity values while automatically using them, which reduces user visibility over account linkage and report history access.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists a default user and returned tokens in a workspace SQLite database and may reuse an existing data/smyx-api-key.txt identity; no system-level autorun or backdoor persistence was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Remote pet video analysis and cloud report lookup match the stated purpose, but the implementation adds automatic identity resolution, silent account registration, token storage, and account-scoped history retrieval.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending pet videos or video URLs to the configured cloud service and with the skill automatically creating or reusing an internal account identity, storing tokens in workspace data, and using that identity to fetch historical reports. This is not classified as malicious, but the identity and persistence behavior deserves review before use.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: The local identity and token-handling behavior is real and materially broadens the skill beyond media analysis, even though parts of it are documented in the skill instructions.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The code can call a silent registration/login endpoint and save returned token material locally; this supports Review because the user is not clearly put in control of account creation or reuse.
[SQP-2] expected: Uploading local media or passing video URLs to server APIs is expected for this cloud analysis skill, but users should be clearly aware that household pet imagery and metadata may leave the local workspace.
[SDI-1] expected: Historical report listing is described in SKILL.md, but it depends on the same hidden identity flow and returns account-scoped cloud records.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill lacks tight permission scoping around network calls, local file reads, output writes, and workspace identity storage.
[YR4] unexpected: The detected zero-width characters appear to be normal emoji joiners in visible table text, not hidden instructions, so this signal was downgraded.
[P9] unexpected: The whitespace findings correspond to code formatting and did not reveal concealed instructions during inspection.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese output strings are visible and consistent with the package language, but users should expect Chinese-language CLI messages and reports.
